study type: Prospective longitudinal population-based birth cohort study
cohort: Pregnant women residing in Brno or Znojmo regions in the Czech Republic, expected to deliver between March 1991 and June 1992
finding: Better self-rated health during pregnancy was associated with fewer childbirth complications, lower odds of cesarean delivery, and fewer maternal health problems up to 3 years after delivery.
mod_finding: Better self-rated health during pregnancy was associated with lower odds of cesarean delivery (odds ratio 0.81; P=0.003).
